cases.name: scalars-of-each-type
cases.notes: §2.1: one scalar row per key, typed by the YAML value.
cases.source:
---
s: canon
n: 3
f: 1.5
b: true
b2: false
z: null
---

# T

cases.name: nested-map-dotted-keys
cases.notes: §2.3: a mapping recurses with a dotted prefix; the mapping's own key emits nothing.
cases.source:
---
meta:
  owner: alice
  team:
    name: x
    size: 2
---

# T

cases.name: scalar-array-list-rows
cases.notes: §2.3: an all-scalar array is one card=list row per element, ord = index.

cases.name: mixed-scalar-array-typed-per-element
cases.notes: §2.3: elements are typed individually per §2.1.

cases.name: array-of-objects-json-escape-hatch
cases.notes: §2.3: an array containing a mapping is ONE card=list row, ord 0, type json, val_json = the whole array.

cases.name: nested-arrays-json-escape-hatch
cases.notes: §2.3: an array containing an array (or a scalar beside a mapping) is a single json row.

cases.name: empty-map-and-array-vanish
cases.notes: §2.3 / §8: `a: {}`, `b: []` and the nested `c.d: {}` produce no rows; `c.e` and `f` do.

cases.name: arrays-of-empty-containers-are-json
cases.notes: §2.3: `[[]]` and `[{}]` are not all-scalar, so each is one json row carrying the array verbatim.

cases.name: range-numeric-inclusive-and-exclusive
cases.notes: §2.2: type stays string, val_text verbatim, val_json carries {__range, lo, hi, exclusiveEnd}.

cases.name: range-open-ended
cases.notes: §2.2: one bound may be empty (null in the side channel); `1.5...` is an open-ended EXCLUSIVE range (the left bound `1.5` does not end in `.`; the operator is the maximal 3-dot run). `..` alone is not a range (see non-ranges).

cases.name: range-decimal-negative-exponent
cases.notes: §2.2 numeric domain: `^-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?$`; bounds become numbers.

cases.name: range-date-and-datetime
cases.notes: §2.2 ISO domain: bounds stay strings; `T` or space separator; optional seconds/fraction/zone.

cases.name: non-ranges-stay-plain-strings
cases.notes: §2.2: mixed domains, non-scalar bounds, no bounds, a 4-dot run, a plain decimal (quoted, so it is a string), and `1..2..3` (right part `2..3` is not numeric) are ordinary strings with no val_json.

cases.name: range-in-list-elements
cases.notes: §2.2 applies per element: the range-shaped elements get a side channel, `a..b` does not.

cases.name: dotted-key-collision-nested-wins
cases.notes: §1 / §8: an authored `meta.owner` and a nested `meta: {owner}` flatten to the same key; the later row in parser order wins on prop_id.
cases.source:
---
meta.owner: a
meta:
  owner: b
---

# T

cases.name: dotted-key-collision-authored-wins
cases.notes: §8: same collision, reversed authoring order — the later (authored dotted) row wins.
cases.source:
---
meta:
  owner: b
meta.owner: a
---

# T

cases.name: non-string-keys-stringify
cases.notes: §2.3 / §4: non-string YAML keys are their string spellings. Rows are sorted by key so JavaScript's integer-key-first object order does not show.

cases.name: null-key-is-empty-string
cases.notes: §4: a `null` key becomes key "".

cases.name: tilde-key-is-empty-string
cases.notes: §4: `~` is null, so the key is "".

cases.name: unicode-keys-and-values-sort-bytewise
cases.notes: §7: keys sort bytewise (UTF-8): `emoji`, `t\xc3\xadtulo`, `zeta`.

cases.name: crlf-fence
cases.notes: §3.1: CRLF line endings inside and around the fence.

cases.name: closing-fence-trailing-whitespace
cases.notes: §3.1: the closing `---` may carry trailing whitespace (the block's raw ends `---   `; the YAML text drops that whole line).

cases.name: empty-frontmatter-has-no-rows
cases.notes: §3.1: `---\n---` parses to null, not a mapping — no frontmatter rows (and no body).

cases.name: blank-line-frontmatter-has-no-rows
cases.notes: §3.1: a fence around a blank line is null YAML — no frontmatter rows; the body still computes $title.

cases.name: frontmatter-only-document
cases.notes: §7: a document that is only a fence — no body blocks, no computed rows.

cases.name: frontmatter-only-no-trailing-newline
cases.notes: §3.1: the closing fence without a final newline is still the frontmatter block.

cases.name: invalid-closing-fence-has-no-rows
cases.notes: §3.1 / §8 Fixed: `---bar` does not close the fence, so the tree is a thematic break + a paragraph and there is no frontmatter block — no `foo` row. The old regex over the raw source produced one.

cases.name: yaml-line-starting-with-dashes-is-inside-the-fence
cases.notes: §3.1 / §8 Fixed: the fence closes at the bare `---` line; `---x: 2` is an ordinary key. The old regex cut the YAML short at `\n---x`, dropping it.

cases.name: four-dash-line-is-not-a-fence
cases.notes: §3.1: `----` closes nothing, so the tree is thematic break + setext heading + heading: no frontmatter block, no frontmatter rows.

cases.name: bom-prefixed-document
cases.notes: §3.1: the BOM is leading trivia; the frontmatter block still parses. (The old regex missed it and fell back to the block — same rows either way.)

cases.name: leading-blank-line-means-no-frontmatter
cases.notes: §3.1: the fence must open the document; after a blank line `---` is a thematic break and `a: 1\n---` a setext heading — no frontmatter rows, no H1.
